**Order executed:** Buy 44 AAPL @ limit $222.90 — filled at $222.90 (≈$9,807.60, under the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps; ~0.1% above the $222.70 market price).

**Summary:** I read Apple's just-filed FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024), checked the news, and confirmed the quote, then bought 44 shares of AAPL at $222.90. The headline financial fact is that Apple's **net income declined to $93,736 million in fiscal 2024 from $96,995 million in fiscal 2023** — but almost entirely because of the one-time, non-cash-like $10.2 billion net income tax charge from the European Commission State Aid Decision, which pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% from 14.7%. Underneath that, the business improved: total net sales rose 2% to $391,035 million (FY2023: $383,285 million), operating income grew to $123,216 million from $114,301 million, gross margin expanded to 46.2% from 44.1%, Services revenue jumped 13% to $96,169 million at a 73.9% gross margin, and operating cash flow was a robust $118,254 million, funding $95.0 billion of buybacks and $15.2 billion of dividends. So the earnings dip looks like a tax artifact rather than operating deterioration. News flow was neutral-to-slightly-positive and not a reason to refrain: iPhone 16 supplier builds were described as steady into December, analysts left holiday-quarter estimates unchanged, and shares were "little changed" around $220–222 through the morning (live feed showed a drift from ~$221.8 down to ~$220.4 before recovering to $222.70). With the stock consolidating near its recent range alongside a record-revenue, higher-margin franchise, I viewed a modest starter position as justified within the mandate; the order is buy-only, well under the $10,000 single-order limit, requires no cash movement out of the account (cash was $50,000), and leaves total same-day purchases at $9,807.60 against the $20,000 cap.
